text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Thousands of Finns live in flats inaccessible to rescue workers in emergency; fire brigade equipment does not reach or access is otherwise blocked.
- Freedom of speech to replace freedom of press in legislative reform which also aims to reduce bureaucratic control on the media.
- Finland's oldest security firm, family-owned Suomen Vartioimis ja Sulkemis Oy sold to Danish Falck. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Introduction of euro will boost Finnish forest industry acquisitions in central Europe, says Matti Korhonen, managing director of forest industry lobby.
- Municipalities face use of two currencies in EMU -- they as public authorities will have to use euro while individuals will still use markka.
- Kerta Oy, struck by paper worker strikes last week, would have moved its equipment to Estonia had a settlement not been reached, managing director says. @
- Finland's clothing wholesalers clearly underperformed the trade sector due to bad weather in all seasons, lobby says.
AAMULEHTI
- United States NATO ambassador Robert Hunter says NATO's doors remain open to Finland even after the summit in Madrid this summer.
- Possession of child pornography and buying under-age sex to become punishable offenses in new criminal law. @
TURUN SANOMAT
Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) and Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) start talks on common position on conditions for joining EMU.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Ever more Finnish exporters maintain competitive prices by employing sub-contractors in Estonia and Russia.
- Food poisoning kills man at Niuvanniemi hospital outside Kuopio in northern Finland and 95 others ill -- problem is probably restricted to the hospital, doctors say. @
- Trend to increase short-term employment must not continue, says Lauri Ihalainen, chairman of the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).
